data.title: reloads.sh: launch staging in socket automation mode with the QA flag, and scrub C11_SURFACE_ID/WORKSPACE_ID from the app env

data.body:
# C11-219: reloads.sh: launch staging in socket automation mode with the QA flag, and scrub C11_SURFACE_ID/WORKSPACE_ID from the app env

Found during the 0.65.1 staging smoke (2026-09-11). (1) A Release staging app has fresh defaults, so socket control comes up in c11-only ancestry mode and every CLI call from outside that instance fails with 'Failed to write to socket'; the orchestrator had to relaunch by hand with C11_SOCKET_ENABLE=1 C11_SOCKET_MODE=automation. reload.sh already passes these for dev builds (line ~500); reloads.sh should too, and honour C11_QA_LAUNCH the same way launch-tagged-automation.sh does. (2) reloads.sh's OPEN_CLEAN_ENV unsets the CMUX_* and C11_TAB_ID/C11_PANEL_ID vars but not C11_SURFACE_ID, C11_WORKSPACE_ID, C11_SURFACE_NUM, so a staging app launched from inside c11 inherits the launcher's surface identity (verified with ps eww). Add them (and their CMUX_ twins) to the list in reloads.sh and reload.sh.

## Plan

1. Update `scripts/reloads.sh`'s staging launch environment to scrub the complete C11/CMUX surface identity set while preserving the script-owned socket paths. Launch the Release staging app with `C11_SOCKET_ENABLE=1` and `C11_SOCKET_MODE=automation`, and forward the QA launch value with the same primary/legacy semantics as `QALaunchPolicy` and `launch-tagged-automation.sh` so `fresh` suppresses both startup modals and `resume` remains an explicit opt-in.
2. Add the missing `C11_SURFACE_NUM` and `CMUX_SURFACE_NUM` entries to the existing clean environment lists in `scripts/reloads.sh` and `scripts/reload.sh`, retaining each script's deliberate tag-specific socket assignments and existing dev behavior.
3. Leave `scripts/reloadp.sh` unchanged: it is the untagged production Release launcher, has no isolated staging socket or tagged QA mode, and changing it would broaden the production launch contract beyond C11-219.
4. Update `skills/c11-hotload/SKILL.md` to document that tagged staging sockets are externally reachable in automation mode and how the staging launcher carries `C11_QA_LAUNCH`; do not sync installed skills.
5. Validate shell syntax and, after the required provisioning, run one lock-wrapped Release staging build from inside c11 with inherited identity sentinels. Prove the tagged socket answers `c11 ping` and `c11 tree` from outside the staging instance, startup dialogs are suppressed, and `ps eww` contains none of the scrubbed identity variables. Quit the staging app and remove its DerivedData. Report the exact commands, timings, and any `reload.sh` validation limitation; then commit, push, open the PR, and wait for green CI.

# C11-219 validation report

## Delivered

- `scripts/reloads.sh` now clears inherited `C11_*` and `CMUX_*` surface, workspace, surface-number, tab, and panel identity before launching a tagged Release/staging app.
- `scripts/reloads.sh` injects `C11_SOCKET_ENABLE=1`, `C11_SOCKET_MODE=automation`, the staging `C11_SOCKET_PATH`, and the staging `CMUXD_UNIX_PATH`.
- `scripts/reload.sh` also clears inherited C11/CMUX surface-number identity.
- `skills/c11-hotload/SKILL.md` documents external staging CLI access and `C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh|resume` pass-through.
- `scripts/reloadp.sh` was not changed by C11-219. The C11-218 `assert-ghosttykit.sh` call remains in `reload.sh`, `reloads.sh`, and `reloadp.sh`.

## Local proof

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `bash -n scripts/reloads.sh scripts/reload.sh scripts/reloadp.sh scripts/launch-tagged-automation.sh` passed.
- From a c11 terminal, ran Release staging with sentinel values for all C11/CMUX identity variables and `C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh`.
- The locked staging build completed with `** BUILD SUCCEEDED **` in 662 seconds.
- From an external shell, `C11_SOCKET_PATH=/tmp/c11-c11-219-staging-launch-env-proof.sock c11 ping` returned `PONG`.
- External `c11 tree --no-layout` returned the ready staging workspace.
- The staging process contained `C11_SOCKET_ENABLE=1`, `C11_SOCKET_MODE=automation`, and `C11_QA_LAUNCH=fresh`; no C11/CMUX identity sentinels remained.
- The staging app quit cleanly; its process, socket, c11d socket, and `/tmp/c11-staging-c11-219` DerivedData were removed.

The local runtime proof ran before the later C11-218 rebase. After rebasing, the exact-head shell/diff checks passed again and the hosted CI below ran on the rebased head.

## Exact-head integration

- Main was refreshed to C11-218 `6e9d45a1a`; the branch was rebased cleanly and force-pushed.
- Final branch head: `eb39e54d424c3788c9b8d042e88599e83c9021f4`.
- Final `origin/main` and merge-base: `6e9d45a1aa3cd8c169cd34ca08a03dde71b605d9`.
- PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/441
- Fresh exact-head workflows all passed: CI (`34742501161`), Build GhosttyKit (`34742501198`), Drawbridge (`34742499741`), and macOS Compatibility (`34742501164`).

No merge, deployment, or installed-skill sync was performed. The ticket is ready for orchestrator review.

PASS. PR #441 squash-merged on a head rebased onto the C11-218 merge. reloads.sh now launches staging with C11_SOCKET_ENABLE=1 and C11_SOCKET_MODE=automation, passes C11_QA_LAUNCH through, and scrubs the full C11/CMUX surface, workspace, surface-number, tab and panel identity; reload.sh gains the surface-number scrub. reloadp.sh deliberately unchanged (untagged production launcher). Delegator proved it on a real lock-wrapped Release build launched from inside c11 with sentinel identity vars: external ping returned PONG, external tree answered, ps eww showed automation mode and QA fresh with no identity sentinels, then quit and cleaned DerivedData. Skill doc updated; orchestrator syncs it.
